biography.html: Ross Munro is a New Zealand clothing entrepreneur who founded Gulf Star Products with his wife, Marilyn, before acquiring the Line 7 brand. Born in Rotorua and educated at Waikato University, he later owned and led Canterbury's Australasian businesses. His subsequent interests include sports merchandise and the outdoor clothing brand Swazi.

long_biography.plain_text:
Clothing entrepreneur Ross Munro worked with artist Dick Frizzell and art dealer John Gow to turn New Zealand imagery into Rugby World Cup merchandise. His Sportfolio business collaborated on a range using Frizzell's designs, including a new cartoon character and a motif inspired by half-time oranges. The artwork appeared on T-shirts and hoodies, as well as limited-edition prints.

At Swazi, Munro concentrated on making the outdoor brand easier for European retailers to stock. He established a UK distribution facility and worked with dealers to understand which products they could sell. The business broadened its range while retaining the distinctive look developed by founder Davey Hughes.

confidence.reason: Full original reporting identifies collaboration, artist authorship, motifs and products. Direct owner interview supports specific distribution and range decisions without forecasting commercial success.
